headline: High-risk interaction: ctx can observe Claude Code events and filesystem while LlamaFactory is local-only, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure if outputs are bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse and Stop events and has filesystem access, so if LlamaFactory outputs are copied into that channel, injected instructions could be reinterpreted. LlamaFactory itself has no file or MCP I/O, so the bridge is indirect, but the shared content path is plausible.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory output is manually pasted into ctx-observed Claude Code sessions, injected instructions can propagate.
IF ctx parses file or tool output as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Treat all copied model output as untrusted text.
Disable automatic parsing of tool output as instructions.
Use a fixed prompt template that quotes pasted content.
Review ctx hooks for instruction-like patterns before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between LlamaFactory output and ctx inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content, while LlamaFactory exposes no filesystem, network, or clipboard surfaces. That makes direct leakage from B to A unlikely; the main risk is local workspace exposure if operators manually move sensitive text into ctx-managed files.
conditions: IF sensitive data is placed in a shared local file that ctx reads, ctx may retain it in logs.
IF operators paste secrets from LlamaFactory into ctx-managed artifacts, those secrets can enter audit/runtime logs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared files.
Rotate or redact logs before sharing them.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Verify LlamaFactory remains fileless and offline.
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can write via filesystem-adjacent workflows and install packages, but LlamaFactory explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP. There is no overlapping write surface in the profiles, so conflict is limited to unusual operator-mediated handoffs rather than default contention.
conditions: IF an operator gives both agents the same writable directory through an external wrapper, file contention can occur.
IF ctx is extended with additional write targets outside the profile, conflicts may emerge.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git repo.
Serialize any manual handoff steps.
Confirm LlamaFactory stays read-only.
requires-engineering: add lock coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx can observe tool events and logs, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative context for downstream actions. LlamaFactory is a customer-support model with no verification or action-taking controls shown, so if its text is forwarded into ctx workflows, errors can cascade across work products even without direct automation.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory-generated text is forwarded into ctx without human verification, mistakes can propagate.
IF ctx uses observed events as ground truth, incorrect summaries can be reused downstream.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse.
Mark LlamaFactory output as draft only.
Add a verification checklist for ctx outputs.
Separate factual extraction from action execution.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and confidence metadata.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, so compliance risk is limited to the fact that ctx handles audit/runtime logs while LlamaFactory exposes no such data handling. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is undocumented, uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ctx audit/runtime logs, retention obligations may apply.
IF LlamaFactory is used on regulated content and its outputs are archived elsewhere, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in logs.
Set short log-retention windows.
Document data-class handling for both agents.
Review deployment region and retention settings.
requires-engineering: align formal compliance controls across the pair.
